- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1723-1725 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: URL-container detection only inspects up to 32 characters preceding the issue path for a github.com/ host prefix. When a repository-scoped issue path appears inside a query parameter or fragment of an enclosing non-GitHub URL (such as https://example.com/?next=owner/repo/issues/42 or https://example.com/#see-owner/repo/issues/43) or another repository's URL, host_prefix does not match and url_start falls back to match.start(). When the enclosing URL's fragment precedes the issue path, the tail after the issue number contains no # character, causing the issue number to be extracted as a linked issue.
  WHY: If a PR description references an external link or another repository's URL that carries a repo-scoped issue path in an anchor fragment or query parameter, extract_repo_scoped_issue_refs_from_text incorrectly extracts the issue number. Workflows using this helper can treat the referenced issue as linked and inappropriately apply state transitions or labels.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1734-1737 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The Markdown destination scanner treats every closing parenthesis ) at depth zero as terminating the link destination, without checking whether the parenthesis is escaped with a backslash (\).
  WHY: In GitHub-flavored Markdown destinations containing backslash-escaped parentheses followed by a fragment, such as [link](https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/12?q=a\)b#issuecomment-1), the scan breaks at the escaped \) rather than continuing to the true destination terminator. The trailing #issuecomment-1 fragment is excluded from the tail, causing issue 12 to be extracted as a linked issue.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1720-1726 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The URL-container detection only recognises a `github.com/` host prefix. For a repo-scoped issue path that appears inside the query or fragment of any other URL host (e.g. `https://example.com/?next=owner/repo/issues/42`, `https://example.com/#see-owner/repo/issues/43`, or `<a href="https://example.com/?next=owner/repo/issues/42">`), `host_prefix.search` returns `None`, so `url_start` falls back to the start of the issue path itself. The forward scan then covers only the path forward, not the enclosing URL. The issue number is added to `found` because no `#` appears in the tail after the digits.
  WHY: A PR body that cites a non-GitHub URL whose query or fragment contains a `<repo>/issues/<n>` path will still have that issue extracted as a linked issue. Callers (`issue_pr_status.yml`, `review_autofix.yml`'s identical-failure cap, `review_collect_pr_metadata.sh`, `review_rb_judge.sh`) can then label the issue `ai:merged` / `ai:review-blocked` or finalize its lineage based on a citation that lives inside another URL. The doc comment (lines 1661-1680) explicitly promises "an issue path inside its query or fragment is part of it, never a link of its own" for "Each URL/path" — the implementation does not fulfil this for non-`github.com` hosts. The accompanying test module has no regression assertion for this shape, so CI stays green while the contract is unmet (Copilot review comment 4154749577).
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1732-1742 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The Markdown-destination parenthesis scanner treats every `)` at depth zero as the destination terminator, including a backslash-escaped `\)`. GitHub-flavoured Markdown permits escaped parentheses in link destinations, so a URL such as `[c](github.com/owner/repo/issues/12?q=a\)b#issuecomment-1)` (or with `https://` and a path that ends in a `\)`) has its destination terminated at the escaped parenthesis before the `#issuecomment-1` fragment. The forward scan stops there, the tail contains no `#`, and `issue 12` is added to `found`.
  WHY: A PR body that uses a Markdown link with a backslash-escaped parenthesis in the URL and a `#` fragment after it returns the issue number as a linked issue even though the URL points at a comment. The contract is "any `#` fragment disqualifies the URL", but the depth scan stops before reaching the fragment when the destination contains `\)`. The test module has no assertion for an escaped-paren destination, so CI passes while the contract is unmet (Copilot review comment 4154749621). In practice this is rare (GitHub users almost always percent-encode parentheses in URLs), but the failure mode is concrete: a backslash-escaped paren in the query of an issue URL defeats the fragment filter.
- Requirement: "A URL or path that carries a `#` fragment points at something inside the issue … so it is not a linked issue (issue #5776). Each URL/path is taken whole, the way GitHub renders it as one link … a repo-scoped issue path inside its query or fragment is part of it, never a link of its own." (helper doc comment at scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1661-1680)
  Expected change site: scripts/gh_helpers.sh, the `extract_repo_scoped_issue_refs_from_text` python3 scan (the `host_prefix`/`url_start` block, lines 1720-1726) and its regression assertions in tests/test_issue_pr_status_comment_url_links.py
  Evidence of absence: The `host_prefix` regex matches only `github.com/` (with optional `https?://` or `www.`), so any non-`github.com` URL host whose query or fragment contains `<repo>/issues/<n>` still has that path extracted as a linked issue. The new test module covers github.com URLs (e.g. `test_issue_path_inside_a_url_query_or_fragment_is_not_a_link` at lines 159-187) but has no assertion for `https://example.com/?next=<repo>/issues/<n>` or `https://example.com/#see-<repo>/issues/<n>`, and the doc comment's "any URL" promise is not enforced for those inputs.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: The Markdown destination scanner must respect GitHub-flavoured Markdown's backslash-escape rules for parentheses in link destinations, so a `\)` inside the URL does not terminate the destination early and a `#` fragment after it still disqualifies the URL.
  Expected change site: scripts/gh_helpers.sh, the parenthesis depth-tracking loop (lines 1732-1742), and tests/test_issue_pr_status_comment_url_links.py
  Evidence of absence: The depth-tracking loop matches `(` and `)` blindly without accounting for a preceding `\` escape. The Copilot-flagged case `[c](github.com/owner/repo/issues/12?q=a\)b#issuecomment-1)` is not asserted by any test in the new module; CI therefore passes while the contract ("any `#` fragment disqualifies the URL") is not enforced for escaped-paren destinations.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
